questions.question: An ambulance siren emits at $f_0 = 800\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and moves toward a stationary observer at $v_s = 34\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Speed of sound $v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find the frequency heard by the observer.
questions.answer:
Doppler formula: $f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$

Source approaching, observer stationary: use $v + v_o = v$ (no observer motion), $v - v_s$ in denominator:

$f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v - v_s} = 800 \times \dfrac{340}{340 - 34} = 800 \times \dfrac{340}{306}$

$= 800 \times 1.111 = 888.9 \approx 889\ \mathrm{Hz}$

Approaching source $\Rightarrow$ higher pitch.

questions.question: The same ambulance from the previous problem is now moving **away** from the observer at $v_s = 34\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find the observed frequency.
questions.answer:
Source moving away: denominator uses $v + v_s$:

$f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v + v_s} = 800 \times \dfrac{340}{340 + 34} = 800 \times \dfrac{340}{374}$

$= 800 \times 0.9091 = 727.3 \approx 727\ \mathrm{Hz}$

Receding source $\Rightarrow$ lower pitch.

questions.question: A stationary source emits $f_0 = 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$. An observer moves toward the source at $v_o = 17\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Then the observer moves away at the same speed. Find both observed frequencies. ($v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.answer:
**Observer moving toward stationary source:**

$f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v + v_o}{v} = 500 \times \dfrac{340 + 17}{340} = 500 \times \dfrac{357}{340} = 500 \times 1.05 = 525\ \mathrm{Hz}$

**Observer moving away from stationary source:**

$f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v - v_o}{v} = 500 \times \dfrac{340 - 17}{340} = 500 \times \dfrac{323}{340} = 500 \times 0.95 = 475\ \mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: State and derive the Doppler formula for sound: $f' = f_0\dfrac{v + v_o}{v - v_s}$, where $v_o$ is the observer speed (positive toward source) and $v_s$ is the source speed (positive toward observer). Include sign convention.
questions.answer:
**Wavelength emitted:** The source emits $f_0$ cycles/second. As the source moves toward the observer at $v_s$, each wavefront is "compressed": the effective wavelength seen ahead of the source is:

$\lambda' = \dfrac{v - v_s}{f_0}$ (compressed wavelengths ahead of approaching source)

**Frequency received:** The observer moving toward the source at $v_o$ intercepts wavefronts at rate:

$f' = \dfrac{v + v_o}{\lambda'} = \dfrac{(v + v_o)f_0}{v - v_s}$

$$f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v + v_o}{v - v_s}$$

**Sign convention:**
- $v_o > 0$ when observer moves **toward** source (increases $f'$)
- $v_s > 0$ when source moves **toward** observer (decreases denominator, increases $f'$)
- Reverse signs for motion away.

questions.question: A train horn sounds at $f_0 = 600\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The train moves at $v_s = 20\ \mathrm{m/s}$ toward a wall. What frequency does the wall reflect back to the train driver? ($v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.answer:
**Step 1 — Frequency received by the wall** (wall = stationary observer, source approaching):

$f_\text{wall} = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v - v_s} = 600 \times \dfrac{340}{320} = 637.5\ \mathrm{Hz}$

**Step 2 — Frequency heard by train driver** (wall = stationary source at $f_\text{wall}$, driver = moving observer, approaching wall):

$f' = f_\text{wall} \cdot \dfrac{v + v_o}{v} = 637.5 \times \dfrac{340 + 20}{340} = 637.5 \times \dfrac{360}{340} \approx 675\ \mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: A source emitting $f_0 = 1000\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and an observer are both moving. The source moves toward the observer at $v_s = 20\ \mathrm{m/s}$, and the observer also moves toward the source at $v_o = 10\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find $f'$. ($v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
A police siren of $f_0 = 900\ \mathrm{Hz}$ is observed as $f' = 950\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Is the police car approaching or receding? Find its speed. ($v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.answer:
$f' > f_0 \Rightarrow$ source is **approaching** the observer.

$f' = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v - v_s}$

$v - v_s = \dfrac{f_0 v}{f'} = \dfrac{900 \times 340}{950} = \dfrac{306000}{950} \approx 322.1\ \mathrm{m/s}$

$v_s = 340 - 322.1 = 17.9 \approx 18\ \mathrm{m/s} \approx 64.8\ \mathrm{km/h}$

questions.question: A source moves at $v_s = 170\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (half the speed of sound, $v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$) and emits $f_0 = 400\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Find the frequency heard: (a) ahead of the source, (b) behind the source.
questions.answer:
**(a) Ahead (source approaching observer):**

$f'_{\text{ahead}} = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v - v_s} = 400 \times \dfrac{340}{340 - 170} = 400 \times \dfrac{340}{170} = 400 \times 2 = 800\ \mathrm{Hz}$

**(b) Behind (source receding from observer):**

$f'_{\text{behind}} = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v + v_s} = 400 \times \dfrac{340}{340 + 170} = 400 \times \dfrac{340}{510} = 400 \times \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 267\ \mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: Two trains approach each other. Train A emits $f_A = 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and moves at $v_A = 30\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Train B moves at $v_B = 10\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find the frequency heard by the engineer of Train B. ($v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.answer:
Source = Train A approaching, Observer = Train B approaching the source:

$f' = f_A \cdot \dfrac{v + v_B}{v - v_A} = 500 \times \dfrac{340 + 10}{340 - 30} = 500 \times \dfrac{350}{310}$

$= 500 \times 1.129 \approx 564\ \mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: A source of frequency $f_0$ is moving in a circle of radius $R$ with period $T_\text{circle}$. An observer is far away along the plane of the circle. Describe qualitatively the range of frequencies the observer hears and explain the maximum and minimum.
questions.answer:
The source velocity relative to the observer oscillates sinusoidally. When the source moves **directly toward** the observer (tangential velocity = maximum approach speed $v_s = 2\pi R/T_\text{circle}$):

$f'_{\max} = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v - v_s}$ (highest pitch)

When moving **directly away**:

$f'_{\min} = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v + v_s}$ (lowest pitch)

When moving **perpendicular** to the line of sight ($v_s$ component = 0):

$f' = f_0$ (no Doppler shift at these moments)

The observer hears a smoothly varying pitch cycling between $f'_{\min}$ and $f'_{\max}$ at the frequency of the source's circular motion — this is how astronomers detect orbiting stars (spectroscopic binaries) via Doppler shifts in their spectral lines.
